feature1.prompt: In the current documentation process for type aliases, there is inconsistent behavior where some multiline docstrings are not displayed correctly. For one type alias the docstring appears as intended, while for others only a default 'alias of …' message is shown. This indicates that the mechanism for retrieving the actual docstring attached to a type alias is not working uniformly. The solution should ensure that the complete docstring for a type alias is correctly extracted and made available for use during documentation generation.
feature1.hint_texts: This feature focuses on introducing a dedicated method to extract variable comments from type aliases. It requires implementing a new API that will retrieve the associated docstring or comment data from the source. The implementation should use module analysis techniques to look up the comment, handle any errors gracefully (for example, catching exceptions like PycodeError), and return the comment as a list of string lines if available or return None when absent.
feature1.entrypoint: Modify the file sphinx/ext/autodoc/__init__.py by adding a new method named get_variable_comment. The implementation should be placed after the existing get_doc method. This method must utilize ModuleAnalyzer.for_module to analyze the module and access the attribute documentation via analyzer.attr_docs using an appropriate key based on the object's path. Implement the necessary error handling and ensure the method returns the expected values.

tests.FAIL_TO_PASS: No explicit failing tests provided for the standalone extraction functionality of get_variable_comment.
tests.PASS_TO_PASS: Existing tests should eventually confirm that get_variable_comment retrieves the correct comment for type aliases when a docstring is provided, and returns None when no comment is present.

feature2.prompt: The documentation generation for type aliases currently shows a default 'alias of …' message when a multiline docstring exists for some aliases, leading to inconsistent output. The intent is to have the full, user-provided docstring appear in the rendered documentation rather than the default alias message. Modifications are needed so that when a type alias has an associated docstring, it overrides the default behavior and displays the complete documentation as intended.
feature2.hint_texts: This feature involves integrating the new comment extraction API into the existing documentation generation workflow. Update the behavior of the get_doc method so that it calls the get_variable_comment method and, based on its output, determines whether to output the default alias text or not. Also, modify the add_content method to conditionally suppress the default 'alias of …' message if a valid doc-comment is present. The changes should ensure that type aliases with docstrings consistently display the full content.
feature2.entrypoint: Edit the file sphinx/ext/autodoc/__init__.py in two places. First, in the get_doc method, incorporate a call to get_variable_comment to check for an existing comment and return an empty list when a comment is found, thereby preventing the default output. Second, update the add_content method so that it only appends the default alias message if get_variable_comment returns None. These modifications must be aligned so that the overall behavior of type alias documentation is improved.

collaboration_points.shared_resources: Both features modify the sphinx/ext/autodoc/__init__.py file. They share the new get_variable_comment API as well as the documentation generation methods get_doc and add_content. The ModuleAnalyzer and its attribute documentation structure are central components used by both features.
collaboration_points.integration_strategy: Feature1 will provide a standalone extraction mechanism for variable comments, while Feature2 will integrate that mechanism into the broader documentation pipeline. It is essential that the output and error handling of get_variable_comment are well understood and consistently used in get_doc and add_content to ensure uniform behavior across type aliases.
collaboration_points.communication_needs: Developers working on each feature should coordinate on the expected return values and error scenarios for get_variable_comment. Ensure that any changes in the extraction logic are communicated and that the integration in the documentation generation process correctly interprets these values. Regular discussions on test cases and integration points will help maintain consistency in the final solution.
